# What KEEL covers

<!-- Generated by tools/coverage-doc.mjs from the code. Do not edit by hand: run `node tools/coverage-doc.mjs`. A test fails when this file is out of date. -->

For every kind of Microsoft 365 setting, this page says whether KEEL backs it up, what KEEL can restore, how well that restore is proven, and what you do yourself.

KEEL tracks 179 kinds of Entra ID and Intune settings and backs up everything it can read of each one. 45 are full, 127 incomplete, 7 Microsoft-managed and 0 not readable. KEEL can restore 98 at least in part; the other 81 are restored by hand from the backup.

## How to read this page

- **Backed up:** every kind listed here is backed up. The tier sets how often, on the default schedule (an operator can change it).
- **Coverage:** one of four states.
  - *Full:* KEEL restores it on its own and nothing is missing.
  - *Incomplete:* the backup holds everything KEEL can read, but some parts cannot be brought back automatically. It is recreated from the backup, by KEEL or by hand, and the missing parts are listed below the table as follow-up steps. Each backup flags the incomplete objects it holds.
  - *Microsoft-managed:* Microsoft owns it, so there is nothing to restore.
  - *Not readable:* KEEL cannot read it, for the reason given.
- **KEEL can restore:** what a KEEL restore does. "By hand" means a person restores it from the backup, for the reason given below the table. "Not built yet" means KEEL backs it up in full and will recreate it on its own once that restore is built.
- **Proof:** "Tested against a simulated tenant" means the restore code has passed tests against a fake Microsoft service. It is not yet proven on a live tenant. A failed live test is listed with its date until a fix passes.
- **Microsoft limit:** Microsoft offers no way for any tool to do this. KEEL cannot work around it; the steps say what to do instead.
- **KEEL choice:** KEEL could write it, but leaves it to a person for safety or because part of it is not backed up.

### Details and what you do

- **Users.** Puts reviewed user details back, brings deleted users back from the recycle bin, adds missing licences, and recreates a permanently deleted user with sign-in off and a checklist of what the person needs.
  - *Not brought back:* password (Microsoft never returns it); registered sign-in methods, such as MFA (Microsoft never returns it); details synced from on-premises Active Directory (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* A recreated user needs a new password or Temporary Access Pass and must register MFA again, because Microsoft never lets anyone read them; KEEL lists these as follow-up items and leaves sign-in off until then. Users synced from on-premises Active Directory are restored there, and guests are invited again.
- **Groups.** Recreates groups, puts their settings back, removes groups added since the backup, brings deleted groups back, and restores members and owners.
- **Organizational contacts** (Microsoft limit). These contacts come from directory sync, and Microsoft makes them read-only for every tool.
  - *You do:* Restore them at their source, usually on-premises Active Directory or Exchange, and let sync bring them back.
- **App registrations.** Recreates app registrations, puts their settings back, and brings deleted ones back from the recycle bin.
  - *Not brought back:* client secrets (Microsoft never returns it); certificates (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Microsoft never lets anyone read client secrets or certificates, so after a recreate create new ones and update every service that used them. KEEL lists these as follow-up items. Removing extra apps is done by hand.
- **Enterprise apps.** Recreates an enterprise app for its app registration, puts reviewed settings back on an existing one, and removes an app added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* client secrets (Microsoft never returns it); certificates (Microsoft never returns it); whether sign-in is on, which a restore reports and never changes (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Whether an app can sign in is shown as a difference and changed by hand. Enterprise apps for Microsoft services and managed identities are never removed by KEEL.
- **Delegated app consents.** Grants delegated consent again with the permissions the backup had, as part of an approved restore, and changes a consent back. A re-run never adds a second consent.
  - *You do:* Removing a consent added since the backup is done by hand. A consent for an app that was recreated in the same restore is granted by hand.
- **External identity providers** (Microsoft limit). Microsoft never lets anyone read the client secret of an identity provider.
  - *Not brought back:* client secret (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Recreate the provider in the Entra admin center using the settings in the backup, and enter a fresh secret from the provider.
- **Certificate sign-in settings** (not built yet). A wrong certificate trust setting can lock everyone out, and KEEL has no safe way to test the change first.
  - *You do:* Restore the certificate authorities by hand in the Entra admin center using the backup, and test sign-in before closing the session.
- **Built-in admin roles** (Microsoft limit). Microsoft provides the built-in roles. They are switched on from Microsoft's templates, never written.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore. Who holds each role is restored with role assignments.
- **Custom admin roles.** Recreates custom roles and puts their permissions back. The dry run lists permissions a restore adds and removes.
  - *You do:* Built-in roles cannot be changed by anyone. Custom roles need an Entra ID P1 or P2 licence. Removing extra custom roles is done by hand.
- **Admin role templates** (Microsoft limit). Microsoft publishes these templates. They are the same in every tenant.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore.
- **Admin role assignments.** Recreates admin role assignments, changes them back and removes ones added since the backup.
- **Eligible admin roles.** Makes people eligible for an admin role again, keeping the original end date.
  - *Not brought back:* changing or removing an eligibility, and ones inherited through a group (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Expired eligibilities and ones inherited through a group are not restored. Changing or removing an eligibility is done by hand.
- **Time-limited active admin roles** (not built yet). Restoring a time-limited active role safely needs an expiry check and a guard against replaying a past activation. That is not built yet. Permanent assignments are covered by admin role assignments.
  - *Not brought back:* activations people made themselves (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup to see who held which role until when, then assign it again in Privileged Identity Management.
- **Admin role activation settings.** Puts activation rules back: how long a role lasts, what activation needs, and who approves.
  - *You do:* A restore that would weaken protection waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID. Approvers must still exist.
- **Role-to-settings links** (Microsoft limit). Entra links exactly one settings policy to each role itself. Nobody writes the link.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore. The settings are restored with admin role activation settings.
- **Access reviews** (not built yet). The history and decisions of past reviews cannot be recreated by anyone. Only the review setup could be, and KEEL has not built that yet.
  - *Not brought back:* past reviews and their decisions (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Recreate the review in the Entra admin center using the setup in the backup. Keep the backup as the record of past decisions.
- **Access packages** (not built yet). An access package depends on its catalog, policies and resource roles, which are backed up but not restored yet.
  - *You do:* Recreate the package in Entra ID Governance using the backup as a guide, starting with its catalog.
- **Connected organizations** (not built yet). These point to other organizations' tenants, which KEEL cannot check from yours.
  - *Not brought back:* internal and external sponsors (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate them by hand in Entra ID Governance using the backup.
- **Lifecycle workflows.** Recreates workflows with their tasks and puts their settings back. A recreated workflow is always off.
  - *Not brought back:* run history and the users each run processed (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Turning a workflow on runs its tasks on people's accounts, so a restore turns it on only after a second person approves it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID. Check who it applies to before approving.
- **Lifecycle workflow extensions.** Recreates extensions and puts their settings back.
  - *Not brought back:* the Logic App it calls (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Make sure the Logic App each extension calls still exists in its Azure subscription.
- **Lifecycle workflow settings.** Puts the settings back.
- **Custom security attribute sets.** Puts the description and size limit of an existing set back.
  - *Not brought back:* an attribute set that no longer exists, which needs a review before it is created (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* An attribute set can never be deleted once it exists, so a missing one is recreated by hand after a review, in the Entra admin center.
- **Custom security attributes.** Puts the description and status of an existing attribute back, and adds or turns off its allowed values.
  - *Not brought back:* the values assigned to users and apps (stored separately and not in the backup yet); an attribute that no longer exists, which needs a review before it is created (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* An attribute can never be deleted once it exists, so a missing one is recreated by hand after a review, inside its attribute set. Values assigned to users and apps are not backed up.
- **Access package catalogs.** Recreates catalogs and puts their settings back.
  - *Not brought back:* the groups, apps and sites in the catalog (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* The groups, apps and sites a catalog holds are not backed up yet, so add them again by hand.
- **Access package policies** (not built yet). A policy belongs to an access package, and access packages are not restored yet.
  - *Not brought back:* approval and request history (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Recreate the access package first, then its policies, using the backup.
- **Access package assignments** (not built yet). Access is granted through a request against a policy, never copied, and access packages are not restored yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the original request and its approval (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup to see who held which access package, then assign it again in Entra ID Governance.
- **Entitlement management settings.** Puts the settings back.
- **Terms of use** (not built yet). The agreement documents are files that are not backed up yet, and nobody can recreate who accepted them.
  - *Not brought back:* the agreement documents (a file the backup does not hold); who accepted the terms (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Upload the documents again and recreate the terms of use in the Entra admin center using the backup. Users will be asked to accept again.
- **Guest sign-up user flows** (not built yet). The languages, attributes and API connectors a flow uses are not backed up yet.
  - *Not brought back:* its languages, sign-up attributes and API connector links (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate the user flow in the Entra admin center using the backup.
- **API connectors for user flows** (not built yet). The password or certificate a connector uses can never be read back.
  - *Not brought back:* password or certificate (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Recreate the connector using the backup, and enter its password or certificate again.
- **Provisioning and cross-tenant sync jobs** (not built yet). A job's attribute mappings are stored separately, its sign-in details can never be read back, and a running job changes accounts in another directory.
  - *Not brought back:* its attribute mappings (the sync schema) (stored separately and not in the backup yet); the sign-in details for the target app, if it uses any (Microsoft never returns it); run history and current status (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Set up provisioning again on the enterprise app using the backup as a guide, check its mappings, then start it.
- **Access package resource roles** (not built yet). A role can only be added once its group, app or site is in the package's catalog, and access packages are not restored yet.
  - *You do:* Recreate the access package first, then add the same groups, apps and sites with the roles in the backup.
- **Custom authentication extensions** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Recreate the extension in the Entra admin center from the backup, then check that its endpoint still answers. Sign-ins and workflows that call it need it back first.
- **Access review settings.** Puts back whether group owners can manage access reviews of their groups.
- **Admin role access review defaults.** Puts back the default settings of access reviews of admin roles.
  - *You do:* Reviews already running keep the settings they started with.
- **User flow attributes** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the custom attributes but does not restore them yet. The built-in attributes are set by Microsoft.
  - *Not brought back:* built-in attributes (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Recreate each custom attribute in the Entra admin center, under External Identities, Custom user attributes, from the backup, before the user flows that collect it.
- **Authentication event listeners** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. Each one points to a custom authentication extension.
  - *You do:* Recreate the custom authentication extension first, then the listener with PowerShell from the backup, for the same apps.
- **Exchange admin roles** (KEEL choice). KEEL backs up the custom roles. Microsoft offers no way to create them outside Exchange, so KEEL recreates a custom role that is gone through Exchange Online PowerShell, from its parent role, with the same entries (the Exchange admin role restore, off until its live proof passes). It never changes a role that still exists. The built-in roles are set by Microsoft.
  - *Not brought back:* built-in roles (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* For a custom role that still exists but differs from the backup, the restore lists what differs: fix its entries with Exchange Online PowerShell. Then give recreated roles back to their role groups or apps, after a privilege review.
- **Exchange admin role assignments** (not built yet). KEEL backs up who holds each Exchange role and over which scope, but does not restore them yet. Admin access needs a privilege review first.
  - *You do:* Check the backup with the person who approves admin access, then add the role groups, people or apps again in the Exchange admin center, under Roles, Admin roles, or with Exchange Online PowerShell.
- **Exchange app access scopes.** Recreates scopes and puts back their name and which mailboxes they cover (the recipient filter).
  - *Not brought back:* the app role assignments that use it (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* An app role assignment points to its scope by id and is not restored: point the assignment at a recreated scope again with Exchange Online PowerShell.
- **Defender admin roles.** Recreates custom Defender roles and puts back their name, description and permissions.
  - *Not brought back:* a built-in Defender role (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Who holds each role is not restored: add the assignments again in the Microsoft Defender portal, under System, Permissions, Microsoft Defender XDR, Roles, after a privilege review.
- **Defender admin role assignments** (not built yet). KEEL backs up who holds each Defender role and for which data sources, but does not restore them yet. Admin access needs a privilege review first.
  - *You do:* Check the backup with the person who approves admin access, then add the assignments again in the Microsoft Defender portal, under the role, Assignments.
- **Defender app access scopes** (Microsoft limit). KEEL backs these up, but Microsoft offers no way for a tool to create or change them.
  - *You do:* Recreate each scope by hand from the backup, before the assignments that use it. There is no admin center page for it.
- **App certificate authority trust** (not built yet). KEEL backs up which apps have a certificate authority trust list, but not the authorities on it, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the trusted certificate authorities (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Create the configuration again with PowerShell, then add the same certificate authorities from your own copies.
- **Verified ID profiles** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each verification profile's accepted issuer, claims and Face Check setting but does not restore it yet.
  - *You do:* Create the profile again in the Entra admin center, under Verified ID, from the backup.
- **Entitlement management outside connectors** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each connector to resources outside Entra ID but does not restore it yet.
  - *You do:* Create the connector again with PowerShell from the backup.
- **PIM custom extensions** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each extension's name and how it signs in, but not the Logic App address it calls, which can hold an access key. It does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the Logic App address it calls (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Create the extension again in the Entra admin center, under Privileged Identity Management, and pick the same Logic App.
- **PIM managed groups** (not built yet). KEEL backs up which groups are managed by Privileged Identity Management. A group comes back under it when it gets its first eligible member.
  - *You do:* Add an eligible member to each group again in the Entra admin center, under Privileged Identity Management, Groups.
- **Entitlement management role assignments** (not built yet). KEEL backs up who is a catalog owner, catalog reader or access package manager, and over which catalog, but does not restore it yet.
  - *You do:* Add the same people to the same roles in the Entra admin center, under Identity Governance, Entitlement management, from the backup.
- **Device templates** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each device template's maker, model and operating system but not its owners or the devices made from it, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* its owners and the devices made from it (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Create the template again with PowerShell from the backup, then add its owners.
- **Teams custom apps** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each app your organisation uploaded to Teams, with its versions and publishing state, but not the app package, which Microsoft does not give out. It does not restore them yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the app package (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Upload the app package again in the Teams admin center, under Teams apps, Manage apps, from your own copy, then check its details against the backup.

### Details and what you do

- **Conditional Access policies.** Recreates policies, puts their settings back, removes ones added since the backup, and brings deleted ones back. Every write lands in report-only mode.
  - *You do:* Turning a restored policy on is a separate, approved step that first checks the break-glass accounts can still sign in.
- **Authentication strengths.** Recreates custom authentication strengths and puts their settings back.
  - *Not brought back:* a change to the allowed sign-in method combinations (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Built-in strengths cannot be changed by anyone. A change to the allowed sign-in method combinations is reported, not restored: set it by hand. Removing extra strengths is done by hand.
- **Named locations.** Recreates named locations, puts their settings back and removes ones added since the backup.
- **Authentication contexts** (not built yet). Each context has a fixed slot that Conditional Access policies and SharePoint labels point to. KEEL cannot yet check what uses a slot before changing it.
  - *You do:* Restore the name and description by hand in the Entra admin center, keeping each one in the same slot as in the backup.
- **Authentication methods.** Puts the authentication methods policy and each method's settings back, only when the break-glass accounts can still sign in afterwards.
  - *You do:* A method that no longer exists in your tenant is not added back.
- **Security defaults.** Turns security defaults on or off as in the backup, only when the break-glass accounts can still sign in afterwards.
- **User and guest permissions.** Puts guest invitation, self-service, consent and default user permission settings back, only when the break-glass accounts can still sign in afterwards.
- **Cross-tenant access.** Puts the list of allowed Microsoft clouds back.
- **Cross-tenant access defaults.** Puts the default tenant restrictions and guest sign-in order back.
  - *You do:* Inbound trust (accepting another tenant's MFA and device claims), automatic consent and the guest collaboration and direct connect lists are never changed by a restore. If they differ from the backup, change them by hand in Cross-tenant access settings.
- **Cross-tenant access per organization.** Recreates partner organization entries and puts their tenant restrictions back.
  - *You do:* A partner tenant that no longer exists cannot be added. Removing extra partners is done by hand. Inbound trust, automatic consent and the guest collaboration and direct connect lists are never changed by a restore; change them by hand if they differ.
- **Device join and registration settings** (KEEL choice). These settings decide who may join devices and whether joining needs MFA. A wrong write could stop admins joining devices or quietly drop the MFA requirement, so KEEL only backs them up.
  - *You do:* Compare the backup with the current settings in the Entra admin center under Devices, and change them there.
- **External user self sign-up.** Puts back whether external users may sign themselves up.
  - *You do:* The sign-up user flows themselves are restored by hand (see guest sign-up user flows).
- **App consent policies.** Recreates custom app consent policies and puts their name and description back. When the backup holds their include and exclude rules, it puts those back and removes rules added since the backup (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* the include and exclude rules of a custom policy (stored separately and not in the backup yet); a built-in app consent policy (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Microsoft's built-in policies cannot be changed by anyone. Rules the backup does not hold yet are set by hand.
- **Admin consent requests.** Puts the admin consent request workflow back, including who reviews requests.
- **Idle sign-out policy** (not built yet). The whole policy is backed up, but KEEL does not yet tell a tenant-wide policy from one set on a single app, so it has no safe restore yet.
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate the policy by hand using the backup.
- **Token claims mapping.** Recreates the policy and puts its name and settings back (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet); being the organization default (KEEL recreates it as an ordinary policy) (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps use the policy is set again by hand. A policy that was the organization default comes back as an ordinary one; make it the default again by hand after checking it.
- **Sign-in routing (home realm discovery).** Recreates the policy and puts its name and settings back (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet); being the organization default (KEEL recreates it as an ordinary policy) (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps use the policy is set again by hand. A policy that was the organization default comes back as an ordinary one; make it the default again by hand after checking it. Test a federated sign-in after the restore.
- **Token issuance policy.** Recreates the policy and puts its name and settings back (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet); being the organization default (KEEL recreates it as an ordinary policy) (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps use the policy is set again by hand. A policy that was the organization default comes back as an ordinary one; make it the default again by hand after checking it.
- **Token lifetime policy.** Recreates the policy and puts its name and settings back (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet); being the organization default (KEEL recreates it as an ordinary policy) (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps use the policy is set again by hand. A policy that was the organization default comes back as an ordinary one; make it the default again by hand after checking it.
- **Staged rollout of sign-in features** (not built yet). Which groups a rollout covers is stored separately, and KEEL has not built a safe writer for it.
  - *Not brought back:* which groups the rollout covers (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate the rollout by hand using the backup, then add the same groups.
- **App credential policies.** Recreates the policies and puts their rules back.
  - *Not brought back:* which apps the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps each policy applies to is not backed up yet, so assign the policies again by hand.
- **Default app credential rules** (not built yet). A stricter default can stop every app from adding a secret or certificate, so KEEL will not write it without a review step, which is not built yet.
  - *You do:* Set the default rules again in the Entra admin center using the backup.
- **Multitenant organization.** Puts the name and description back.
  - *Not brought back:* each member tenant's acceptance (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Member tenants and their acceptance are set by each tenant, so add or re-invite them by hand.
- **Cross-tenant sync per organization** (not built yet). These settings let a partner tenant sync its users into yours, so KEEL will not write them without a review step, which is not built yet.
  - *You do:* Set the partner's sync settings again in the Entra admin center under cross-tenant access settings, using the backup.
- **External user leave settings.** Puts back whether external users can leave your organization themselves, and whether their data is removed when they do.
- **Guest invitation domain restrictions** (KEEL choice). KEEL backs up the list of domains guests may, or may not, be invited from, and shows when it changes. A restore never changes who can be invited.
  - *You do:* Set the domains again in the Entra admin center, under External Identities, External collaboration settings, Collaboration restrictions.
- **App creation policies** (Microsoft limit). KEEL backs up each policy with its include and exclude conditions, but Microsoft only lets a signed-in admin change these policies, not an app like KEEL.
  - *Not brought back:* a built-in app creation policy (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Recreate a custom policy and its conditions with PowerShell from the backup, signed in as an Entra admin. There is no admin center page for it. Built-in policies are Microsoft's and cannot be changed.
- **App permission pre-approval policies.** Puts back which app permissions are pre-approved, and where (chats, teams or the whole organization).
  - *Not brought back:* which app it is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* A policy only works once it is assigned to its app. Assign a recreated policy to the app again with PowerShell.
- **Multitenant organization sync template.** Puts back the user sync settings a tenant gets when it joins your multitenant organization.
  - *You do:* Tenants that already joined keep their own settings; change those per organization.
- **Multitenant organization access template.** Puts back when the template applies to tenants that join your multitenant organization.
  - *Not brought back:* its cross-tenant access settings (trust in partner sign-ins, automatic consent, who may cross) (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Which partner users and apps get in, automatic consent, and trust in partner MFA and devices are never changed by a restore: set them by hand. Tenants that already joined keep their own settings.
- **Guest SAML or WS-Fed sign-in.** Puts back each partner's name and sign-in protocol.
  - *Not brought back:* its domains (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* KEEL never puts back a partner's sign-in addresses or signing certificate, so a changed backup cannot send guests to another sign-in page. Check those with the partner and set them in the Entra admin center, under External Identities, All identity providers. A deleted partner is set up again there too, with its domains.
- **Attack simulation automations** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each automation's name and status but does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* each run of the automation (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate the automation in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Email and collaboration, Attack simulation training, Automations, from the backup.
- **Attack simulations** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each simulation's settings and targets but not its results, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the payload, landing page and login page the simulation uses (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Launch the simulation again in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Email and collaboration, Attack simulation training, Simulations, with the same technique, payload and targets from the backup.
- **Sign-in identifiers** (not built yet). KEEL backs up which identifiers people can sign in with (email, user name, custom user name) and whether each is on, but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Turn the same identifiers on or off in the Entra admin center, under External Identities, from the backup.
- **Lifecycle policies** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each lifecycle policy's scope, grace period and action (such as disabling accounts that stopped signing in), but not its rules or past versions, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* its rules and past versions (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Create the policy again in the Entra admin center, under Identity Governance, Lifecycle workflows, from the backup, and leave it off until you have checked who it covers.
- **Default cross-tenant sharing settings** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the default calendar sharing, mail tips and room booking settings for other tenants but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Set the same values with PowerShell from the backup.
- **Defender custom detection rules** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each custom detection rule: its hunting query, schedule, alert details and response actions. It does not restore them yet.
  - *Not brought back:* past runs and the alerts a rule raised (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Create the rule again in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Hunting, Custom detection rules, from the backup. Leave it off until you have checked its response actions, because a rule can isolate devices or disable users.

### Details and what you do

- **Tenant profile** (Microsoft limit). This is the tenant itself. Microsoft does not let any tool recreate or replace it.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore. Use the backup as a record of the tenant details at that time.
- **Domains** (Microsoft limit). Adding a domain needs proof that you own it, through a DNS record that only you can publish.
  - *Not brought back:* proof that you own the domain (a DNS record you publish) (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Add the domain in the Microsoft 365 admin center, publish the DNS record it asks for, and verify it. Domains must be back before users and mail that use them.
- **Licence subscriptions** (Microsoft limit). Licences are bought from Microsoft, not configured.
  - *You do:* Use the backup to see which licences you had and how many. Buy or reactivate them before restoring users, because a user restore can only assign licences you hold.
- **Group setting templates** (Microsoft limit). Microsoft publishes these templates. They are the same in every tenant and nobody can edit them.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore.
- **Tenant-wide group settings.** Puts changed tenant-wide group settings back, and removes ones added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* settings on a single group (stored separately and not in the backup yet); a deleted tenant-wide setting (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* A setting that was deleted, and settings on a single group, are recreated by hand from the backup.
- **Company branding.** Puts the sign-in page text, colours and layout back, and uploads the background image, banner logo, square logos, favicon and custom stylesheet again when they changed (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* header logo (a file the backup does not hold); content customization files (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* The header logo, and any file that was not set or was over 1 MB at backup time, are uploaded by hand in the Entra admin center. A tenant with no branding gets none from KEEL.
- **Company branding per language.** Puts the sign-in page text, colours and layout of each existing language back, and uploads its images and stylesheet again when they changed (tested against a simulated tenant only).
  - *Not brought back:* header logo of each language (a file the backup does not hold); adding or removing a language (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* The header logo is uploaded by hand, and a language that was added or removed is added or removed by hand.
- **Group expiration policy.** Puts the policy back. A shorter lifetime, more groups covered or a dropped notice address waits for approval first.
  - *Not brought back:* the list of groups a selected-groups policy covers (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* A missing policy, and the list of groups it covers, are set by hand. A change that could expire and delete groups waits until a second person approves it in Approvals, unless restore approvals are off for Entra.
- **Administrative units.** Puts the name and description back.
  - *Not brought back:* members and admins scoped to the unit (stored separately and not in the backup yet); dynamic membership rules and a deleted unit (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Members, admins scoped to the unit, dynamic membership rules and a deleted unit are restored by hand from the backup.
- **SharePoint and OneDrive tenant settings.** Puts back the tenant-wide SharePoint and OneDrive settings, such as site creation, sync app limits, idle session sign-out, Loop and storage limits. The sharing settings are put back by the SharePoint service backup.
  - *You do:* Turning legacy authentication on, letting devices outside the domain sync, or letting a guest invitation be accepted by another account waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for SharePoint.
- **Item insights setting** (not built yet). KEEL backs up whether people cards and search show the documents a person worked on, and the group it is turned off for, but does not restore it yet.
  - *You do:* Set the same value in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under Settings, Org settings, Search and intelligence, from the backup, and pick the same group again.
- **Copilot connectors** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each connection's name, description and allowed apps but not its schema or the items pushed into it, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the connection schema and the items pushed into it (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Recreate the connector in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under Copilot, Connectors, from the backup, then let it sync its items again.
- **Exposure management zones** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each zone's name and description but not the environments in it, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the environments in the zone (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Create the zone again in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Exposure management, and add the same environments.
- **Shared email domains** (not built yet). KEEL backs up which shared email domains the tenant uses. Microsoft sets them up; there is nothing to restore.
  - *You do:* Ask Microsoft support if a shared domain is missing.
- **Schema extensions** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the schema extensions this tenant's own apps defined, but not the values stored in them on users and groups, and does not restore them yet.
  - *Not brought back:* extensions owned by apps in other tenants (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Create the extension again with PowerShell, with the same id, owner app and properties from the backup.
- **Microsoft Forms settings.** Puts back the tenant-wide Forms settings, such as sharing forms outside the organisation, phishing scans and Bing image search. The forms and their answers are not backed up.
  - *You do:* Widening sharing outside the organisation or turning the phishing scan off waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID.
- **Microsoft To Do settings** (not built yet). KEEL backs up whether To Do lists can be shared with or joined by people outside the organisation, and push notifications, but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Set the same values in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under Settings, Org settings, Microsoft To Do, from the backup.
- **Microsoft 365 Apps installation options.** Puts back which Microsoft 365 apps people can install themselves on Windows and Mac, and the update channel.
- **User owned apps and services.** Puts back whether people can use the Office Store and start app trials.
  - *You do:* Turning the Office Store on waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID.
- **Usage report privacy.** Puts back whether usage reports hide real user, group and site names.
  - *You do:* Showing real names again waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID.
- **Profile card fields** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the extra directory fields shown on profile cards and their labels, but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Add the same fields again with PowerShell (New-MgAdminPeopleProfileCardProperty) from the backup.
- **Pronouns setting.** Puts back whether people can add pronouns to their profile.
- **Viva Engage communities.** Puts back the name, description and privacy of a community that still exists. Its posts, files and members are not backed up.
  - *Not brought back:* a deleted community (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet); posts, files and members of the community (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* A deleted community is created again by hand in Viva Engage with the same name, description and privacy from the backup, then its owners and members. Making a private community public waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Entra ID.
- **Defender for Identity sensors** (not built yet). KEEL backs up which servers have a Defender for Identity sensor and each sensor's settings, such as its description, the domain controllers it covers and delayed updates. It does not restore them yet.
  - *Not brought back:* the sensor software on each server and its health (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Install the sensor again on any server that lost it, then set the same settings in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Settings, Identities, Sensors, from the backup.
- **Secure Score action states** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the state an admin set on each Secure Score action, such as resolved through a third party or risk accepted, with the reason given. It does not restore them yet.
  - *Not brought back:* microsoft's text and score for each action (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Set the same state and reason on each action in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Exposure management, Secure Score, Recommended actions, from the backup.

| Derived credential issuers | Yes (Tier 2, important, daily) | Incomplete | By hand (not built yet) | None |
| Microsoft Tunnel server configurations | Yes (Tier 2, important, daily) | Incomplete | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Microsoft Tunnel health thresholds | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | Yes: put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Apple app provisioning profiles | Yes (Tier 2, important, daily) | Full | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| App dependencies and supersedence | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back; take out a link a restore added, when that restore is undone | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Managed e-books | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | By hand (not built yet) | None |
| E-book categories | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Classroom device cart assignments | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Windows app protection policies | Yes (Tier 2, important, daily) | Full | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| Windows code signing certificates | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | By hand (not built yet) | None |
| Symantec code signing certificate | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | By hand (KEEL choice) | None |
| Endpoint analytics baselines | Yes (Tier 3, low impact, weekly) | Incomplete | Yes: recreate if deleted; put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |
| BIOS configurations | Yes (Tier 2, important, daily) | Incomplete | Yes: put changed settings back | Tested against a simulated tenant |

### Details and what you do

- **Device configuration profiles.** Recreates profiles, puts their settings and assignments back, and removes an unassigned profile added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* passwords, keys and certificates in Wi-Fi, VPN, certificate and email profiles (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Profiles that carry passwords or certificates (Wi-Fi, VPN, certificate, email), and any value Microsoft never returns, are finished by hand. A profile added since the backup that is still assigned is removed by hand.
- **Device compliance policies.** Recreates policies, with their actions for noncompliant devices, puts their settings and assignments back, and removes an unassigned policy added since the backup.
  - *You do:* A policy added since the backup that is still assigned is removed by hand.
- **Settings catalog policies.** Recreates policies, puts their settings and assignments back, and removes an unassigned policy added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* secret settings (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Secret settings are never returned by Microsoft, so enter them again by hand. A policy added since the backup that is still assigned is removed by hand.
- **Enrollment restrictions** (Microsoft limit). The default restrictions exist in every tenant and cannot be created by anyone, and the order of custom ones is set by a separate action KEEL does not write.
  - *You do:* Restore by hand in the Intune admin center from the backup, which includes each restriction's assignments and order.
- **Intune admin roles** (KEEL choice). These roles decide who can manage devices, so a change needs a person to review it. Who holds each role is backed up as Intune admin role assignments.
  - *You do:* Review the roles in the backup and recreate them in the Intune admin center, then assign them again.
- **Device categories.** Recreates categories and puts their names and descriptions back.
  - *Not brought back:* which devices are in the category (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Devices are put in a category when they enroll, which no restore can redo. Devices pick it up at their next enrollment, or an admin sets it on each device.
- **Terms and conditions** (Microsoft limit). Who accepted cannot be recreated: a recreated policy asks every user to accept again.
  - *Not brought back:* who accepted the terms (no tool can write it).
  - *You do:* Recreate the terms by hand from the backup and tell users they will be asked to accept again.
- **Windows Autopilot profiles.** Recreates profiles and puts their settings (out-of-box experience, device name template, language) and who they are assigned to back, keeping each profile's kind.
  - *Not brought back:* the registered device hardware it applies to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target. The registered device hardware is not backed up; devices are imported again from the devices themselves.
- **Security baselines (older format)** (KEEL choice). This older format is preview-only and replaced by the settings catalog, and its settings are stored separately and not backed up.
  - *Not brought back:* the baseline's settings (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Rebuild the baseline in the settings catalog. KEEL restores settings catalog policies.
- **Enrolled devices** (Microsoft limit). A device record is created by the device when it enrolls. It is state, not configuration.
  - *You do:* Nothing to restore. Devices enroll again on their own once enrollment settings are back.
- **Apps.** Adds store apps, web links, Microsoft 365 Apps, Edge and WinGet apps again with their settings and who they are assigned to, and puts changed settings back. Win32 and line-of-business apps come back with their install commands, detection rules and other settings, unassigned. Each app is put back in its app categories.
  - *Not brought back:* the app package (the installer file), which must be uploaded before the app is assigned (a file the backup does not hold); an app synced from Apple Business Manager, managed Google Play or Microsoft, which is synced again there (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Microsoft never returns an app's package (the installer file): upload it again for each recreated Win32 or line-of-business app, then assign it as the restore lists. Intune does not let such an app be changed until its package is uploaded, so a restore lists a step for it instead. Apps from Apple Business Manager or managed Google Play are synced again there; KEEL then puts back who they are assigned to. An uninstall assignment is never written: it removes the app and its data from devices. A category that is no longer in Intune is listed as a step: restore it first. Dependencies and supersedence are restored on their own.
- **App protection policies.** Puts the settings of iOS and Android app protection policies back, recreates them with the apps they protect, and removes an unassigned policy added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* windows Information Protection policies (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* A backup taken before the protected apps were read cannot recreate a policy; take a new backup. Windows Information Protection policies are restored by hand. Windows app protection policies are restored on their own.
- **Managed app configuration.** Puts the settings back, recreates a configuration with the apps it targets, and removes an unassigned one added since the backup.
  - *You do:* A backup taken before the targeted apps were read cannot recreate a configuration; take a new backup.
- **App configuration for managed devices.** Recreates configurations and puts their settings back when the app they configure exists, and removes an unassigned one added since the backup.
  - *You do:* Add the app first. Values Microsoft never returns are entered again by hand.
- **Windows PowerShell scripts.** Recreates scripts and puts the script, its settings and who it runs on back.
  - *You do:* Who a script runs on is put back only when the script is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target. A backup taken before scripts were read in full holds only the settings; take a new backup.
- **macOS shell scripts.** Recreates scripts and puts the script, its settings and who it runs on back.
  - *You do:* Who a script runs on is put back only when the script is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target. A backup taken before scripts were read in full holds only the settings; take a new backup.
- **Remediations.** Recreates your own remediations and puts the detection and fix scripts, their settings, who they run on and their schedule back. Remediations published by Microsoft are left alone.
  - *Not brought back:* remediations published by Microsoft (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* Who a remediation runs on is put back only when it is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target.
- **Custom compliance scripts.** Recreates scripts and puts the script, its settings and who it runs on back, before the compliance policies that use them.
  - *You do:* Who a script runs on is put back only when the script is picked for a restore. A backup taken before scripts were read in full holds only the settings; take a new backup.
- **Assignment filters.** Recreates filters and puts their rules back.
  - *You do:* A filter is never moved to another platform; recreate it by hand if its platform changed.
- **Scope tags.** Recreates your own tags and puts their names back.
  - *Not brought back:* the built-in Default tag (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* The built-in Default tag exists in every tenant and is never written.
- **Windows feature update profiles.** Recreates profiles, puts their settings and who they are assigned to back, and removes an unassigned profile added since the backup.
  - *You do:* Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target.
- **Windows quality update profiles.** Recreates profiles, puts their settings and who they are assigned to back, and removes an unassigned profile added since the backup.
  - *You do:* Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, and each group must still exist in the target.
- **Windows driver update profiles.** Recreates profiles, puts their settings and who they are assigned to back, and removes an unassigned profile added since the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* approved drivers (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Driver approvals are not backed up yet, so approve the drivers again by hand. Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore.
- **Administrative templates.** Recreates templates and puts back which settings are turned on or off, the values entered for them and who the template is assigned to.
  - *You do:* Who a template is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore. A setting from an imported template file needs that file imported first. A backup taken before setting values were read is refused; take a new backup.
- **Imported administrative template files.** Imports a deleted ADMX file again, with its ADML language files, from the backup.
  - *Not brought back:* the ids of the settings in it: Intune gives them new ones, so templates that used them are set up again (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* Intune gives the settings in a re-imported file new ids, so administrative templates that used them are set up again by hand. A file is never changed in place: upload a new version in the Intune admin center, under Devices, Configuration, Import ADMX. A backup taken before the file content was read is refused; take a new backup.
- **Compliance notification emails.** Recreates templates and puts their settings and the message text for each language back.
- **Windows Autopilot devices** (Microsoft limit). Microsoft never returns the hardware hash that registers a device, so no tool can register it again from a backup.
  - *Not brought back:* the device hardware hash (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup as the list of devices. Import each device again from its hardware hash, taken on the device or from your vendor.
- **Intune admin role assignments** (KEEL choice). These decide who can manage devices, so a change needs a person to review it.
  - *You do:* Review who held each Intune admin role in the backup and assign the roles again in the Intune admin center.
- **Apple push certificate** (Microsoft limit). Apple issues this certificate. No tool can upload it from a backup, and a new certificate from a different Apple ID cuts off every Apple device.
  - *Not brought back:* the certificate file (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the Apple ID and expiry date. Renew the certificate at Apple with that same Apple ID and upload it in the Intune admin center before it expires.
- **Mobile threat defense connectors** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. The connection is completed from the partner's console.
  - *Not brought back:* the connection made from the partner console (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Set up the connector again from the partner's console, then turn on the settings the backup shows. Compliance policies that use the partner's threat level need it back first.
- **Device management partners** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. The connection is completed from the partner's console.
  - *Not brought back:* the connection made from the partner console (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Connect the partner again from its console, using the backup for the settings.
- **Compliance partners** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. The connection is completed from the partner's console.
  - *Not brought back:* the connection made from the partner console (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Connect the partner again from its console, using the backup for the settings and the groups it applies to.
- **Remote help partners** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. Onboarding is completed from the partner's console.
  - *Not brought back:* the onboarding made from the partner console (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Onboard the partner again from its console, using the backup for the settings.
- **Exchange on-premises connectors** (Microsoft limit). The connector is a program installed on an Exchange server. No tool can install it from a backup.
  - *Not brought back:* the connector installed on the Exchange server (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the server and settings. Download the connector from the Intune admin center and install it on that server again.
- **Exchange on-premises access settings.** Puts back whether Exchange on-premises access control is on and which groups it covers or leaves out.
  - *You do:* Turning it on could block mail on devices that are not managed, so a restore turns it on only after a second person approves it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Intune.
- **App categories.** Recreates your own categories and puts their names back. The built-in categories come with every tenant and are never changed.
  - *Not brought back:* built-in categories (set by Microsoft); which apps are in the category (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Which apps are in a category is set on each app; add the apps to a recreated category again by hand.
- **Company Portal branding.** Recreates branding profiles for your groups and puts back their name, colours, contact details, links and Company Portal options. The default branding, which every user sees, is put back in place.
  - *Not brought back:* logo images (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Logo images are not backed up: upload them again from your own copy. Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore.
- **Settings catalog compliance policies.** Recreates policies and puts back their settings, actions for noncompliance (block, emails, grace periods) and who they are assigned to.
  - *You do:* Who a policy is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, from backups taken after assignments were read; Conditional Access that requires compliant devices needs it assigned first. A backup taken before the actions for noncompliance were read cannot recreate a policy; take a new backup.
- **Reusable settings groups.** Recreates groups and puts their settings back, before the settings catalog policies that use them.
  - *You do:* A group is never moved to another setting definition; recreate it by hand if that changed.
- **Policy sets.** Recreates sets and puts back their names, the apps and policies in them, and who they are assigned to.
  - *You do:* Every app and policy in a set must be back first with the same id. Who a set is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, from backups taken after assignments were read. A backup taken before the apps and policies in a set were read is refused; take a new backup.
- **Apple Volume Purchase tokens** (Microsoft limit). Apple issues the token. No tool can upload it from a backup, and the token itself is never read.
  - *Not brought back:* the token file (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the Apple ID, organization and expiry. Download a new token from Apple Business Manager with that Apple ID and upload it in the Intune admin center.
- **Apple automated enrollment tokens** (Microsoft limit). Apple issues the token. No tool can upload it from a backup, and Microsoft never returns the token file.
  - *Not brought back:* the token file (Microsoft never returns it); enrollment profiles under each token (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the Apple ID and expiry. Download a new token from Apple Business Manager with that Apple ID, upload it in the Intune admin center, then recreate its enrollment profiles.
- **Managed Google Play connection** (Microsoft limit). The connection is made by signing in to Google. No tool can make it from a backup, and the enrollment codes are not backed up.
  - *Not brought back:* enrollment company codes and QR codes (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the Google account and settings. Connect Managed Google Play again in the Intune admin center with that account, then turn on the same enrollment options.
- **Device cleanup rules.** Puts a rule's settings back when that makes it wait as long or longer before retiring devices.
  - *Not brought back:* a deleted rule, and a shorter wait before devices are retired (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* A deleted rule, and a rule the backup has retiring devices sooner than now, are set by hand in the Intune admin center from the backup, because a shorter wait can retire devices at once.
- **Windows hotpatch update policies.** Recreates policies and puts their settings back.
  - *Not brought back:* who the policy is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Who a policy is assigned to is not backed up yet, so assign it again by hand.
- **Multi admin approval policies** (not built yet). KEEL backs these up but does not restore them yet. They decide which changes need a second admin, so a person should review them.
  - *You do:* Recreate each policy in the Intune admin center from the backup, with the same approver groups.
- **macOS custom attribute scripts.** Recreates scripts and puts the script, its settings and who it runs on back.
  - *You do:* Who a script runs on is put back only when the script is picked for a restore, from backups taken after assignments were read. A backup taken before scripts were read in full holds only the settings; take a new backup.
- **Intune tenant settings.** Puts back the compliance settings, such as how devices with no compliance policy are marked and how long a device may go without checking in. The device cleanup window is put back with the device cleanup rules.
  - *Not brought back:* the Company Portal brand, written as the default branding profile (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Marking devices with no compliance policy as compliant waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Intune. The Company Portal contact details are put back with the default branding profile.
- **Android Enterprise enrollment profiles.** Recreates profiles and puts back their name, description, device name template and Wi-Fi network; the enrollment mode is set when a profile is recreated. A profile on a secured Wi-Fi network is recreated by hand, because the Wi-Fi password is not backed up.
  - *Not brought back:* enrollment token, QR code and Wi-Fi password (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* A recreated profile has a new enrollment token and QR code: make a token in the Intune admin center, under Devices, Enrollment, Android, and hand it out again. Recreate a profile on a secured Wi-Fi network by hand and type the password again.
- **Android work profile enrollment profiles.** Recreates profiles and puts back their name and description.
  - *Not brought back:* enrollment token and QR code (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* A recreated profile has no enrollment token: make one in the Intune admin center, under Devices, Enrollment, Android, and hand it out again.
- **Apple user enrollment profiles.** Recreates profiles and puts their settings back (name, description, which enrollment types users may pick and the default).
  - *Not brought back:* its place in the priority order (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet); who the profile is assigned to (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* A recreated profile goes to the end of the priority order and is assigned to nobody: set its priority and assign it again by hand from the backup.
- **Android work profile connection** (Microsoft limit). The legacy work profile connection is made by signing in to Google. No tool can make it from a backup.
  - *You do:* Use the backup for the Google account and target groups, connect again in the Intune admin center with that account, and turn on the same enrollment options.
- **Derived credential issuers** (not built yet). KEEL backs up the issuer settings but does not restore them yet.
  - *You do:* Set the same issuer, help page and renewal threshold in the Intune admin center, under Tenant administration, Connectors and tokens, Derived credentials, from the backup.
- **Microsoft Tunnel server configurations.** Recreates configurations and puts back their network, DNS servers, routes and port.
  - *Not brought back:* the sites and servers that use it (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* A site points to its configuration by id: point the site at a recreated configuration again by hand.
- **Microsoft Tunnel health thresholds.** Puts back the healthy and unhealthy limits of each health check.
  - *Not brought back:* the default limits (set by Microsoft).
- **Apple app provisioning profiles.** Recreates profiles and puts back their name, description, scope tags, the profile file from Apple and who they are assigned to.
  - *You do:* Who a profile is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, from backups taken after assignments were read. An expired file, or one that expires before the profile in Intune now, is never uploaded: renew it with Apple and upload it in the Intune admin center, under Apps, iOS/iPadOS, App provisioning profiles. A backup taken before the profile file was read is refused; take a new backup.
- **App dependencies and supersedence.** Puts back which app depends on or replaces which, and how (install automatically or detect; update or replace), when both apps are in Intune, including apps the same restore added again. Undoing a restore takes out a link it added.
  - *Not brought back:* the app packages on both ends, added again by hand before the link (a file the backup does not hold).
  - *You do:* An app KEEL cannot add again (a synced app) is added by hand first: a link to a missing app is not written. Intune links only Win32 apps, so a link to any other kind of app is a step for a person. Setting an app to replace another uninstalls the older app on devices, so that needs the separate content approval.
- **Managed e-books** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each book's details but not yet who it is assigned to, and does not restore it yet.
  - *Not brought back:* who the book is assigned to (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Sync the books again from Apple Business Manager in the Intune admin center, under Apps, eBooks, and assign them again from the backup.
- **E-book categories.** Recreates categories and puts their names back.
  - *Not brought back:* which books are in the category (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Which books are in a category is set on each book; add the books to a recreated category again by hand.
- **Classroom device cart assignments.** Recreates cart assignments and puts back their name, description, devices and classes.
  - *Not brought back:* the devices and classes it names (stored separately and not in the backup yet).
  - *You do:* Devices and classes are named by id and are not restored by KEEL: if a device or class was removed, add the cart to the new class again in Intune for Education.
- **Windows app protection policies.** Recreates policies and puts back their settings, the apps they cover and who they are assigned to.
  - *You do:* Who a policy is assigned to is put back only when it is picked for a restore, from backups taken after assignments were read. A backup taken before the apps were read is refused for a recreate; take a new backup.
- **Windows code signing certificates** (not built yet). KEEL backs up each public certificate but does not restore it yet.
  - *You do:* Upload the same certificate again in the Intune admin center, under Tenant administration, Connectors and tokens, Windows enterprise certificate, from the backup.
- **Symantec code signing certificate** (KEEL choice). KEEL backs up the certificate's subject, issuer and expiry but never the certificate file or its password.
  - *Not brought back:* certificate file and password (Microsoft never returns it).
  - *You do:* Upload the certificate again from your own copy in the Intune admin center, under Tenant administration, Connectors and tokens, Windows Symantec certificate, and check its expiry against the backup.
- **Endpoint analytics baselines.** Recreates custom baselines and puts their names back. The built-in baseline is set by Microsoft and never changed.
  - *Not brought back:* built-in baselines (set by Microsoft); the scores taken when it was created (set by Microsoft).
  - *You do:* A recreated baseline takes today's scores to compare against, not the scores it held before; compare against the backup by hand if you need the old ones.
- **BIOS configurations.** Puts back each BIOS configuration's name, description, scope tags and whether every device gets its own BIOS password.
  - *Not brought back:* the BIOS settings file, which can hold the BIOS password (Microsoft never returns it); a deleted configuration (in the backup, but KEEL does not write it yet).
  - *You do:* The settings file is not backed up, because it can hold the BIOS password: a deleted configuration is created again in the Intune admin center, under Devices, Windows, Configuration, BIOS configurations and other settings, with the file from your own copy. Turning per-device BIOS passwords off waits for a second person to approve it in Approvals, unless you turned restore approvals off for Intune.

## Microsoft 365 workloads

KEEL backs up the configuration of these workloads, listed below. It also backs up their content in a separate nightly run at 01:00 UTC, with delta sync and deduplication:

- Exchange Online: mail folders and messages, calendars and contacts, including archive mailboxes.
- OneDrive: files.
- SharePoint: sites, lists and list items, document libraries and files with their versions.
- Teams: teams, channels (standard, private and shared), channel members, tabs and apps. Channel files are covered through the team site in SharePoint.
- Planner and group conversations: plans, buckets and tasks with their details; conversations, threads, posts and attachments.

Teams chat and channel messages are not backed up: Microsoft must first approve the Teams export API for your tenant. Once they are, KEEL can restore a channel's messages into a new channel, "<name> (restored <date>)", with their original authors and times, through Microsoft's message import API. Reactions, cards and live @mentions are not brought back (a mention stays as bold text).

A content scope can narrow the content backup to mailboxes, OneDrives, sites and groups whose names start with a set prefix. Teams has no name filter and is always read in full. The KEEL test tenant uses this to back up only its test content.

Each workload ships switched off. KEEL turns a backup on for your tenant only after a live read from your tenant is checked, and turns a restore on only after a live write and read-back on your tenant is checked, at most 30 days old. A test against a simulated tenant never switches anything on.

### SharePoint settings

**Backed up:**

- SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings
- SharePoint site list
- SharePoint site-level app permission grants
- SharePoint site properties
- SharePoint per-site sharing settings

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings
- Add back: SharePoint site-level app permission grants
- Put back: SharePoint site-level app permission grants
- Add back: SharePoint custom permission levels
- Add back: SharePoint site groups
- Add back: SharePoint site group members
- Add back: SharePoint site collection admins
- Add back: SharePoint role assignments on sites and lists

**You do:** Settings KEEL does not restore are changed by hand in the SharePoint admin center using the backup.

### Teams settings and membership

**Backed up:**

- Team member, guest, messaging and fun settings
- Team members and their roles
- Team list
- Members of the Microsoft 365 group behind a team

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: Team member, guest, messaging and fun settings (switched on only after the restore of SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings is proven)
- Add back: Team members and their roles (switched on only after the restore of SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings is proven)
- Put back: Team members and their roles (switched on only after the restore of SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings is proven)
- Remove extras from: Team members and their roles (switched on only after the restore of SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings is proven)

**You do:** Settings KEEL does not restore are changed by hand in the Teams admin center using the backup.

### Exchange mailbox settings

**Backed up:**

- Mailbox settings (automatic replies, time zone, working hours)
- Mailbox client access settings
- Mailbox hold and retention settings
- Exchange organization configuration

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: Mailbox settings (automatic replies, time zone, working hours) (switched on only after the restore of team member, guest, messaging and fun settings is proven)
- Put back: Mailbox client access settings (switched on only after the restore of team member, guest, messaging and fun settings is proven)
- Put back: Mailbox hold and retention settings (switched on only after the restore of team member, guest, messaging and fun settings is proven)
- Put back: Exchange organization configuration (switched on only after the restore of team member, guest, messaging and fun settings is proven)

**You do:** Settings KEEL does not restore are changed by hand in the Exchange admin center using the backup.

### OneDrive settings

**Backed up:**

- OneDrive site sharing and storage settings

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: OneDrive site sharing settings (switched on only after the restore of SharePoint tenant sharing and site settings is proven)

**You do:** KEEL puts back a OneDrive's own sharing settings, default link type and permission, and guest and link expiry. A setting the backup shows following the tenant's OneDrive default is not pinned on the site. A locked site is never changed or unlocked. The owner, storage quota, sensitivity label and conditional access setting are changed by hand in the SharePoint admin center using the backup. Wider sharing needs a second approver.

### Purview sensitivity labels

**Backed up:**

- Sensitivity label definitions
- Sensitivity label publishing policies

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: Sensitivity label definitions (switched on only after the restore of mailbox client access settings is proven)
- Put back: Sensitivity label publishing policies (switched on only after the restore of mailbox client access settings is proven)

**You do:** KEEL only restores label names and tooltips, and adds labels back to a publishing policy. It never weakens a label or unpublishes one: those changes, and new labels, are made by hand in the Purview portal.

### Exchange mail flow and protection

**Backed up:**

- Accepted domains
- Remote domains
- Mail flow (transport) rules
- Inbound connectors
- Outbound connectors
- Anti-spam (hosted content filter) policies
- Anti-phishing policies
- Anti-malware policies
- DKIM signing configuration

**KEEL can restore:**

- Put back: Outbound connectors (switched on only after the restore of mailbox client access settings is proven)

Safe Links and Safe Attachments are backed up only when the tenant has Defender for Office 365.
